chapter: The Raeburn band: people and touring
title: Substitute pianists and Joe Albany
summary: He stayed off tours, using Ike, Dodo or Joe Albany, a gifted but troubled pianist.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: How long did you play your second time on the band?

We were in San Francisco a few months and then we came down to Hollywood. I stayed with the band except for the times they would go out on tour. When they left town to go on tour, even to another location, out of town, I wouldn't leave town. I'd stay and they would use someone else, Ike or Dodo or Joe--what's his
name, a terrific pianist that everybody gave up on because he was so sick and just recently he returned to New York and I hear he's playing the greatest, he's not sick--Joe Albany. That was his name.
I don't know him at all.

Joe Albany is really a great pianistic talent, jazz, really great, but he was very fucked up in those days. He wasn't dependable, he was very sick; couldn't reach him. It was hard to carry on a decent conversation with him, but the talent was there. I'm so delighted to hear that he's well now, back in New York and playing great, I hear.
Yeah, he was playing a jazz club on Broadway I understand recently, Broadway and 112th--somewhere around there.

of Broadway, about the middle of the block. It's between 113th and 114th, on the west side of Broadway and it's in the center of the block, and I think it's called the West End Restaurant; something like that. It's right in the middle of the block. (West End Cafe)
Mike was playing up there a while ago, Mike Abene.
Right. They have ads on their front windows about all the jazz and artists they have.
It's a high class joint now. ( ? )
That's where Joe plays. We got along fine for the longest time, for years as a matter of fact.
Did he get along fine with everybody?
